sentences.text: Heard Mr. Subhash Jha, learned counsel for the  applicant and Ms. Mahalakshmi Ganapathy, learned APP for the  State.
Mr. R. M. H. Jabali, learned counsel appears and states that  he has instructions to appear for the original first informant.
He is  seeking adjournment for filing an intervention application.
At his  request, today I am adjourning the application.
However, I have  heard the parties for consideration of ad-interim relief.
3. The F.I.R. is lodged by one Poonamchand Sharma.
He  has stated that, he was knowing the present applicant because  their shops were opposite to each other.
The applicant was a friend  of the informant's son Manish.
In March 2020, the informant was  in need of money.
Therefore, he took loan from the applicant to  the tune of Rs.90 lakhs at the interest rate of 1%.
At that time, the  applicant had got one document executed.
It was in the nature of  sale deed.
He had kept that document with himself.
Though the  informant was not agreeable to it, he merely questioned the  applicant as to why that document was executed.
At that time, the  applicant had told him that it was his way of entering into the  transactions.
At that time, the applicant had executed another :

sentences.text: In July 2021 he  raised some amount by selling his land and approached the  applicant to repay the loan.
At that time, the applicant told him  that, there were dues of Rs.1,28,00,000/-.
Since the original  documents were with the applicant, the informant accepted the  conditions put by the applicant.
He raised gold   Rs.1,11,55,000/- and also cash amount of Rs.17,30,000/-.
According to the first informant, this amount was paid to the  applicant.
He requested the applicant for returning the original  documents.
But those documents were not returned.
Instead, the  applicant told him that those documents were lost and he gave  photocopies of those documents.

According to the first informant,
 those documents were the false documents.
In June 2023, the  informant wanted to sell his shop because he was in need of  money.
The applicant came to know about it.
He told the  informant that, he was willing to purchase that shop for  Rs.4,11,00,000/-.
The informant agreed to that proposal.

However, they were issued by one Nitin Bharsakade.
The  informant questioned the applicant.
At that time, the applicant told  him that said Nitin Bharsakade was to finance that transaction for  the applicant.
The informant deposited those cheques in his  account.

sentences.text: That money had come to Manish Sharma's account  from Nitin Bharsakade.
The informant finally realized that the  applicant had not purchased that shop, but he had sold the  informant's shop to Nitin Bharsakade.
The informant asked Nitin  Bharsakade about it.
He accepted that he had purchased that shop  from the applicant for Rs.4,63,00,000 lakhs and that he had also  paid Rs.2 crores to the applicant.

The informant realized that he  was cheated and therefore, he filed this F.I.R.
 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the  F.I.R. is filed with malafide intention to pressurize the applicant.
There are two more F.I.Rs. filed against the applicant in which he
is protected by one final order and one ad-interim order
. He ::: Uploaded on - 15/02/2024 ::: Downloaded on - 15/02/2024 19:15:25  5 of 6 8-aba-424  submitted that the applicant is needlessly harassed.
5. Learned APP produced certain copies of th  agreements which were seized during investigation.
6. I have considered these submissions.
The F.I.R. is not  very clear as to how the informant himself was cheated in that  transaction.
The F.I.R. does not mention that the shop is  transferred in the name of either the applicant or the said Nitin  Bharsakade.

If the applicant had taken the money from Nitin Ashwin Amritlal Jain vs State Of Maharashtra on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45713846/
4  Bharsakade, then perhaps the aggrieved party would be Nitin  Bharsakade and not the present informant.

sentences.text: All these aspects will  have to be explained by the informant through his counsel who  has submitted that he would be filing an intervention application.

Therefore, considering these aspects, the applicant can be  protected by way of ad-interim relief with directions to the  applicant to attend the concerned police station and to co-operate  with the investigation.
7. Hence, the following order.

 6 of 6 8-aba-4  ORDER i) In the event of his arrest in connection with C.R.No.765 of 2023 registered at R.C.F. Police Station, Mumbai, till the next date, the Applicant is directed to be released on bail on his executing P. R. bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one or two sureties in the like amount.
ii) This order shall operate till 03/04/2024.

iii) The Applicant shall attend the concerned Police Station from 04/03/2024 to 07/03/2024 between 1.00p.m. to 5.00p.m. and thereafter as and when called and shall cooperate with the investigation.
iv) Stand over to 03/04/2024.
